text:
I am a housing lawyer. u/grasshoppa1 is correct. When you make a maintenance request, the owner or their agent has a reasonable belief that the need for entry is acknowledged by the tenant. They can not enter, say, a month later, nor can they use entry to do work that isnt necessary, but if they are examining or repairing someone the tenant has called to their attention, provided they are entering in a reasonable timeframe, you have no recourse. 

Legally speaking, your right to sold occupancy is called "quiet enjoyment." This term is often confused to mean silence or noise levels, but the term "quiet" in real estate means "without another person on entity with a claim to the title." Since your lease (and state law) require the landlord to give 24 hour notice of nonemergency entry, this applies to any matter that you have not requested -or- is requested but a delayed response. 

Your remedy if the landlord repeatedly enters without notice in non requested, non emergency matters is being allowed to break your lease and move elsewhere. There is no legal process in which you would recover money. The only extant one is you can get an injunction that serves as a court order the landlord must abide by the lease terms. This is pointless and expensive. 

But here, I hate to say it, is you being upset for nothing. If you want them to give notice prior to entry, then make requests for maintenance in writing and request notice of entry prior to doing so. But frankly, any legal action if they do not would almost assuredly be futile.
label: ANECDOTE

· February 2019 – Pay off CC6 in full and pay half of CC 5

· May 2019 – Pay off CC3 in full

· August 2019 – Pay off CC4 and Auto loan in full 

· September 2019 – Pay off CC8 in full

· June 2020 – Pay off Debt Consolidation loan 2 in full

· September 2020 – Pay off CC10 and Consolidation loan 1 in full

· March 2021 – Pay off CC9 in full

· August 2021 – Pay off CC1 in full

First off I want to say I am so sorry you are in this situation. I am 19 and lived in America all my life, I can't imagine what you're going through. I also want to say YES it is a good idea to get out. You need to get out. 

Now,

Are you an American citizen? If not, do you have a passport, visa, etc that will let you travel here legally? If so, you need to get ahold of that. You also will need your birth certificate, especially if you're not yet a citizen. (If you are, find your social security card too.) Basically any important documents make sure you can access them easily. Everything else is replaceable. I would also take anything important to you personally, as well as electronics, clothes, shoes, basically whatever you can fit into one or two bags. 

You can likely contact the American embassy in the country you're in and ask for help/advice on your situation. You're legally an adult, you can leave your mother and not be branded a runaway. They will probably help you.

Since your boyfriend is willing to support you that is GREAT but you need to make sure you have your own income in case anything should happen (break up, death.) Fortunately since you can stay with him that will give you time to find a job. 

Definitely apply for scholarships, financial aid, all that. You will likely quality for a good amount of money. Look into community college, its cheaper and often more flexible for people who have to work. Night classes, online classes, get your general education out of the way for as little $$ as possible & then you can go onto university. 

As for the initial escape plan, find a one way plane ticket back. This is probably what your money should go to first and foremost. Does your mother leave the house ever? Does she go to work? Try your best to get out and to the airport while she is not home. It will make things a lot easier. 

I'm assuming you don't have a car, and I don't know what kind of public transportation the country you're in has. If you have Uber, or any taxi service, that's probably your best bet. Please be safe about this. Don't hitchhike or endanger yourself further trying to get to the airport. The American Embassy might be able to help you here, though I'm not entirely sure. I've never had to contact them nor do I know exactly what they offer.

This is all I can think of, I hope some more Redditors pull through and offer more advice for you. (And maybe someone with experience with an American embassy) I hope you make it back here safe, I'll be keeping you in my thoughts. Good luck!! <3

text:
It doesn't matter if she chooses to get upset or think it means you don't like her. What matters is that you have a roommate who is overstepping his boundaries and that is not acceptable.

First off, this is an issue with your roommate, not with the girlfriend. Your conversation should be with the roommate, and at no point should you ever have to say anything to the girlfriend. It is unfair to you and it is unfair to the girlfriend who had to be told by someone else other than her significant other.

Secondly, you need to set reasonable boundaries. This should have been done when you first moved in, and it is your fault for not doing so, since you are taking issue to a pretty common problem.

Thirdly, I was a housing coordinator for a major university for several years. Every year, we had about 1200 serious housing conflicts or situations and a quarter (if not more) of these issues were caused by overstayed guests (usually bfs or gfs of a resident). In a majority of those cases, the problem is solved simply by referencing the lease that will have a guest policy. Yours probably does too, and you can share that with your roommate.

Finally, the best way to solve this is to come up with a solution and a plan for that solution that you can present to your roommate. Don't simply tell him there is a problem because that's called whining and it's not productive to living with other people. My suggestion is that you figure out a reasonable number of nights she can stay over (more than once a week, no more than four), and then simply ask the boyfriend to contribute some larger portion for cleaning supplies. Also establish cleaning standards. If she can't clean up after herself, then she is simply not allowed to use the kitchen. That is beyond rude of her. You can also ask her to contribute financially to rent. I lived in a house with a guy who asked his gf to marry him and they approached us and asked if she could pay $150 a month to make it not an issue for her to stay over a lot. Even then, she stayed over, on average, about three nights a week...and she cleaned and contributed to groceries and cleaning supplies. 

Ultimately, you need to understand that you are either living with a good roommate or you aren't. So far, he has shown extreme immaturity and lack of self-awareness and empathy in his inability to see that his girlfriends presence all the time might be annoying to those who pay rent. If you approach him and things don't change or he gets bitchy, then your best option is to find a new housing community as soon as possible.

text:
Budget for it.

I like to budget ~~everything~~ with a clear name to indicate what I am allowed to use it for. I get the same anxiety and "what if" thoughts as you and Bullet Journaling has helped me alot with it.
For example, a budget for one month could look like this:
Activities with friends:
Transportation: 10€
Booze: 20€
Food: 20€
Other 10€

Transportation and other (f.e. entrance fees) can hardly be influenced on. But you can bring your own food/booze if you don't want to eat out. If you stay within your pre set budget it helps feeling less stressed about it.

Also: Buy memories not things.

If the 2$ public transport + 10$ booze buys you one evening of fun with your friends and creates good memories then it's not a waste of money. It's an investment on your mental health. Same with netflix. If a local library doesn't have the film's/series you want to watch you can check beforehand if netflix hast them, write down what you want to watch, make room/time for watching them and pay only for a one month membership and cancel it afterwards.
8$ isn't wasted if you spend it on something you actually enjoy doing. 

Being frugal is great but being unhappy not so much.

text: Your goal shouldn't be to find a best friend. Or at least don't openly admit that it's your goal. That's the same as dating someone and being on the lookout for "the one". Then, if you find that you can carry out a conversation, then try to organize something with that individual (or more people from the club/team/work if you have a good group going). Don't wait to get invited or asked to do things. If you're always waiting to get asked to do something, you may never get invited. It's up to you to ask people to do things.
